This is the first round, so I have no history to learn from. The optimal bidding strategy in a second-price auction with rational bidders is to bid slightly below your true value. This is because bidding your true value leaves you vulnerable to losing out on a profitable opportunity if another bidder bids slightly above you. However, bidding too low risks losing the auction unnecessarily. Since my value is $9, I will bid slightly below, say $8.9.

This is a single-round auction. The Nash Equilibrium strategy for this type of auction (second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values) is to bid truthfully. Therefore, I should bid my true value.
